findings.claim: The r5 tests are weaker than the row. test_opencode_rule_matches_the_claude_rule skips the byte comparison when .claude/rules/<rule>.md is absent, which it is on any checkout without an install. test_opencode_rules_come_from_both_install_recipes rejects only a `.claude/rules/*` glob, so a recipe that also copies an eighth rule by name (for example minimal-comments.md) still passes, though the row's fails_when names "a rule outside the 7 is copied".

The .gitignore comment above the whitelist still says it tracks only the project rules that govern tracked content (the .okf bundle, the docs layout, the Terraform layout). slop-scan-for-docs is now tracked for another reason, because APM cannot install a plain .md from a third-party repo, so the comment no longer covers what the block does.

README says apm.yml carries "the rest of the agent tooling" and that caveman is "the one thing APM cannot install". slop-scan-for-docs is a second thing APM cannot install, and it is committed in .claude/rules, not declared in apm.yml.

verdict.text: The migration does what the plan asks.
apm.yml pins the 12 skills to the exact `current.sha` that aim.lock.toml recorded, and the 6 rules and 2 subagents to 1c3dd31.
aim.toml, aim.lock.toml and the AGENTS.md markers are gone, and CLAUDE.md is still a symlink to AGENTS.md.
The MCP entries are out of .mcp.json.
Both install recipes copy the 7 rules by name and remove the two subagents.
The pre-commit exclude covers the installer's paths.
My own stamp is green, including r8 on a clean checkout.
The three findings are a test I want stronger and two doc sentences that are now slightly wrong.
None needs another review.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: "stamp green: 5644de5fc33e662e53238f80e82da8274e3ad930965a7702de91558264ff464d".
Gates pre_commit and cli_tests passed, and rows r1 to r8 passed.
I read the r8 log.
A real `apm install --frozen` installed 23 dependencies, `kmctl plugin patch` ran, then the cp and rm lines ran, and check-install exited 0.
Because .claude/rules is gitignored, the clean run rebuilds the .opencode/rules copies from a fresh install, so a clean git status shows that the committed OpenCode rules match what APM installs.
Pins: compared each skill ref in apm.yml with `[skill.current] sha` in `git show HEAD:aim.lock.toml`.
All 12 match.
r1 to r7: read cli/tests/test_agent_tooling.py.
Each test asserts its row's fails_when, with the gaps noted in f1.
The r7 test also checks that every `just X` the section names is a real justfile recipe.
r9 (judgment): ran `diff -r` myself between the snapshot and the worktree's .claude/skills for all 12 skills.
11 are empty.
python-review differs only by a `.DS_Store` in aim's copy.
That is macOS Finder metadata, ignored by .gitignore, and not skill content, so I count r9's skill half as met.
The rules and subagents diff is recorded at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-vscode-workspace/bb29ac4a-7b6b-458a-a055-0c05909aba19/scratchpad/aim-to-apm-r9-diff.txt.
It shows the expected front matter changes (name and description dropped, `paths: **/*.py` on python-testing) and the newer python-testing body from 1c3dd31.
The scratchpad does not last, so the builder has to pass that diff to the operator in its report.
r9 passes.
r10 (judgment): .okf/decisions/0025-the-agent-guidelines-stay-in-agents-md.md covers the choice and names moving the guidelines into a rule as the rejected option, with the reason.
Its claim that "all but five" files in .claude/rules are gitignored is true after this change.
r10 passes.
Consistency: grepped the tree for aim, drawio-mcp, excalidraw and caveman.
Every remaining aim reference is about `_lazy.py` being copied from aim's code, which is still true.
`kmctl check` reports "all checks passed".
f1 (test-strength, non-blocking): the r5 byte comparison is conditional, and nothing stops an extra named rule in the cp line.
Make the comparison unconditional, or skip with a reason only when .claude/rules was never installed.
Also assert that the set of `.claude/rules/*.md` names in each recipe equals the 7.
r8 already covers byte identity on a clean checkout, so this is not blocking.
f2 (docs, non-blocking): extend the .gitignore comment to say why slop-scan-for-docs is tracked.
f3 (docs, non-blocking): reword the README so it says slop-scan-for-docs is committed in the repository, or limit "the one thing" to plugins.
The primary checkout still has `.claude/plugins/aim-10ae737f6885d841/` and a caveman entry in `.claude/settings.json`, as well as aim's copies under `.claude/`.
These are local, gitignored files, so the worktree diff does not show them.
Plan step 3 has to happen in the primary checkout at land, before `just kmctl-install` runs there.
